title: FP8 enablement: mixed-profile calibration harness and graceful rollback policy for Hopper
creator: Samira Chen
description: Objective: Deliver a repeatable calibration and validation workflow that enables FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) profiles on Hopper GPUs while minimizing customer-facing regressions. Scope includes: build a mixed-profile experiment harness that runs calibration across model families, implement a graceful rollback policy and canary gating in the runtime, and harden numerical stability fixes surfaced during early runs. We will not change model architectures or retrain models — work focuses on quantization profile selection, calibration tooling, runtime guards, and evaluation harnesses.
acceptance_criteria: Automated calibration harness produces per-model candidate profiles (E4M3 and E5M2) with metadata and confidence scores
Validation suite reports relative PPL/EM/ROUGE deltas vs FP32 baseline and flags regressions > 1.5% for downstream metrics
Runtime supports per-route profile pinning and automatic fallback to INT8/FP16 when instability is detected
Canary rollout policy implemented: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with automatic rollback on customer-impacting regressions
Performance telemetry (latency, tail latency, token/second) for FP8 profiles visible in console dashboards
test_plan: Unit tests for calibration pipeline components (scale/zero-point computation, histogram accumulation)
Deterministic calibration runs on benchmark models: Llama-70B, Mistral-7B, internal tuned models
Regression validation: run generation/eval prompts from golden set (1000 prompts) and compare against FP32 baseline
Stress tests on Hopper pools to reproduce observed NaN/instability patterns; run 48h soak tests
Canary deployment to dedicated test tenant with synthetic load and real customer-like prompts
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created after spike showed E4M3 produces slightly better headroom for emergent quantization patterns; initial plan sketched.
2025-02-14: Diego ran initial calibration sweep on Llama-70B. Observed sporadic outlier tokens where scale factor diverged; added histogram clamping stage.
2025-02-16: Added runtime guard: if KV-cache step returns NaN for >0.01% tokens in a batch, fallback to INT8 for that request and increment instability counter.
2025-02-18: First canary experiment (internal only) at 0.5% traffic. Measured +8% token throughput vs FP16 but saw 1.9% delta on ROUGE for summarization suite; flagged for deeper analysis.
2025-02-19: PM review (Ava Park): approved canary gating but requested stricter rollback threshold (1.0% for high-visibility customers). Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-20: Updated calibration harness to emit confidence percentiles and store per-batch histogram snapshots for reproducibility; created PR #2104. Next: expand golden prompt set and run 48h soak on hopper-e4m3 pool.
notes: Trade-offs: E4M3 tends to give slightly better dynamic range for activations but is more sensitive to outliers; E5M2 is more conservative and stable but loses headroom on certain tokens.
Fallback policy rationale: prefer automatic per-request fallback to avoid cross-tenant incidents; maintain aggregated counters to decide when to rollback a profile globally.
Remaining risks: rare NaN patterns correlated with long-context attention resets; engineering is instrumenting KV-cache read/write paths to capture sequence of ops preceding NaN.
Follow-ups: create a one-click console action to force rollback of FP8 profiles for a customer and surface rationale in the incident timeline.
